This is the engineering companion to history.md. It describes the current production pipeline at the last committed checkpoint (2026-11-11): how content is authored, how the firmware is generated and tested, and how the resource budget is enforced. Current contracts remain authoritative in platform.md and dev-flow.md.

1. One fixed build, two board outputs

Sub-hauler has one shipping game configuration. There are no feature profiles, runtime feature selectors, backend selectors or in-game loader rows. The same firmware is built for the Arduboy FX and the Arduboy Mini; only the board target changes.

SurfaceLocationResponsibility
Release entrysub-hauler.inoARDUBOY_NO_USB, setup(), loop()
Shared applicationsrc/app.hppBoot, screen flow, station/flight/story transitions
Pure rulessrc/game.hpp, campaign.hpp, jobs.hpp, chart.hpp, station.hpp, pilot.hppNo Arduino headers; host-testable

Teststst/, tst/fxdatatest/, tools/tests/Permanent, co-located

The DEBUG=1 build is a developer-only map-inspection image. It uses isolated output directories and is not part of the shipped matrix. There is no release variant without the campaign, save, music or splash features.

Core rules are integer-only. Device code uses no float, double, heap allocation, String or dynamic containers. The simulation runs at a fixed 60 Hz; the renderer composes one 1-bit image per frame and presents it with one FX::display(CLEAR_BUFFER).

2. The generation pipeline

make gen is the only shipping generation entry. It runs the asset generators, packs the ordered FX layout and emits the generated headers. It typically writes:

  • fxdata/fxdata.bin — the padded flashable cart image;
  • fxdata/fxdata-data.bin — the unpadded payload;
  • fxdata/fxdata-save.bin — the 4 KiB save partition;
  • fxdata/fxdata.h and the mirrored src/fxdata.h;
  • src/generated/*.hpp — symbolic constants, counts and table accessors;
  • previews under docs/assets/ (terrain, story cards, dock hints, and so on).

make gen-check snapshots the generated set, runs gen again, and fails on any byte change. Generation must be deterministic; a half-generated set is never committed. After a regeneration, stage all generated artifacts together.

Ordered flash ABI

fxdata/fxdata.txt is an ordered declaration list. Declaration order is flash ABI: append new entries, never reorder or remove a shipped one. The file ends with a savesection 4096 marker; the save partition is placed at FX_SAVE_PAGE = 0xFFF0.

There is one documented exception to append-only order: sub-hauler-jxk.1 removed unreferenced legacy tables and retired hull art, and the resulting offset shift is recorded in the commit and platform notes. Do not treat that as a general licence to rewrite the layout. New content is appended before the save section.

The Python tools have their own unittest suites under tools/tests/. Python is never used as a harness to drive the C++ tests; the host tests are compiled and run with the native C++ test framework in tst/.

3. Level and terrain

levels/exploration.json is canonical for the authored map: rooms, passages, gates, coves, settlements and object records. The generator validates connectivity and bounds, emits the packed collision and chart planes, and bakes the static rock into a native 1-bit panorama.

The active terrain image is 2,560 × 1,280 pixels, or 409,600 B in the FX payload. It is stored in the OLED page layout, so the renderer can read visible strips directly into the framebuffer:

  • A page-aligned Y origin reads eight 128-byte strips with FX::readDataBytes.
  • A sub-page Y origin reads the next source page and combines rows in place using AVR hardware multiplication.
  • The final page uses a 32-byte stack scratch for its upper row.
  • There is no second framebuffer, no per-tile draw loop and no clearing pass.

Stations, gates, finds, currents, particles, the boat and the HUD are composed afterward from the same rounded camera origin. Collision remains tile-based; the visual contours and scenery are generated offline and do not change the collision grid. make render-world exports an overview and exact native scene pixels for inspection.

4. Rendering and presentation

The display path is native 1-bit through Arduboy2Base. FRAME(x) is simply x; there is no greyscale or frame-blending path in the shipping build.

src/lib/Blit.cpp draws headerless plus-mask bytes into sBuffer and never touches the OLED. Generated sprite blobs start with a two-byte (width, height) header; SpritesU::drawPlusMaskFX owns that header, while Blit::draw expects the caller to skip it.

The OLED and cart share SPI. Cart reads happen only during update/render, never during the OLED transaction. The frame ends with one FX::display(CLEAR_BUFFER).

The follow camera keeps fractional position in Q4, projects the sub before rounding, and bounds normal corrections to 2 px per tick. Terrain and integer world objects share the rounded origin, so the whole scene scrolls together. The camera uses a small velocity look-ahead; collision still walks one pixel at a time so a faster thruster cannot tunnel through rock.

Runtime UI text is drawn from baked 128×8 plus-mask FX stamps (src/text.hpp, text::stamp/stampFrame). The release image links Arduboy2Base, so the inherited built-in Print/font path is not instantiated; the external font renderer remains reference-test-only. Station rows keep the 7 px pitch and 128×64 clipping. HUD notices are generated rows rather than per-glyph cart reads.

When a function selects a 24-bit FX address or txt_*/img_* constant across branches, assign it to one local and return it once at the end. Repeated return <24-bit>; sites emit duplicate three-byte constant loads. Eight-bit enum selectors are exempt.

5. Rules, views and tests

The pure/device split is the main testability decision:

  • src/game.hpp and the other rule modules know nothing about Arduino, SPI, OLED or input sampling.
  • Host tests compile the same rules and drive deterministic inputs.
  • Views are composed into a plain 1,024-byte framebuffer and compared against expected pixels; the device boundary supplies the real display and cart.

The test pyramid is deliberately layered:

LayerLocationWhat it provesWhat it does not prove
Host C++tst/Rules, state transitions, collisions, save codec, pixel compositionAVR timing, SPI, physical hardware
Toolingtools/tests/Generators, encoding, validation, preview parity, determinismFirmware behavior
Device suitestst/fxdatatest/ via ArdensReal AVR execution, FX reads, SPI, screen pixels, music and stack probesA full manual playthrough
Save-chainmake fxtest-save-chainExact production updateStation() → requestSave() → saveVoyageNow() path with musicPhysical cart wear or power-loss injection
Save runtime pagemake fxtest-save-runtime-pageRuntime FX::programSavePage path, not the compile-time constantHardware; emulator-only
Flight probemake fxtest-flight842 complete flight frames with music, cold caches and camera boundariesWhole-session CPU percentage
Sizemake sizeWhole-image flash and static RAMStack depth; use the painted-stack probe
Docsmake docs-checkLocal links and retired-selector guardsProse accuracy

Tests are permanent and co-located with the code they cover. Device suites are separate fixed .ino sketches that keep USB for serial markers; the release sketch does not. The stack probe paints the free SRAM with 0xA5, runs the real path, scans for the high-water mark, and requires at least 600 B of reserve above __bss_end. Static free bytes alone are not accepted as proof of stack fit.

6. Save system

Voyage checkpoints live in the external FX cart save partition, not the ATmega32u4's internal EEPROM. fxdata/fxdata.txt ends with savesection 4096; the generator emits 4 KiB of erased bytes and FX_SAVE_PAGE = 0xFFF0. FX::begin(FX_DATA_PAGE, FX_SAVE_PAGE) opens both partitions, and every earlier FX offset stays unchanged.

The current schema is 8. It stores a 25-byte scalar payload with a schema signature (0x61), CRC and commit semantics. A save:

  1. erases the 4 KiB block;
  2. programs two 256-byte pages;
  3. writes the commit byte last.

A power interruption may lose the checkpoint; a torn record is rejected and the title offers a clean New Voyage. Untrusted save bytes are validated before use. The retired hull byte stays at its frozen offset and is normalized to HAULER on load. Music is paused around the synchronous erase/program transaction. No save or cart write belongs in the per-frame path.

make gen must be re-run after changing the save section; make gen-check compares the packed image, save partition and header. The EEPROM chart writer and the schema-6 economy fields are retired.

7. Music

Six original underwater loops are authored as atmlib-score v1 JSON under music/. The score sources define tempo, meter, voices, effects and loop length; the generated streams are packed into FX and referenced by symbolic offsets and lengths.

The shipping runtime uses the ATMlib2FX compact synth with ATM_FX_COMPACT_LOOP=1 and ATM_FX_COMPACT_RING=32. The foreground services the FX refill between complete SPI transactions. The sample ISR decodes from SRAM and does not read FX, SPI or the OLED.

Cue selection follows the region and berth; music starts with the first splash and keeps its position through the title. Cue, dock, story and pause transitions switch tracks directly; playtest found the 160 ms fade envelope unpleasant, so the wrapper has no gain ramp. Save pauses the music because the cart transaction is synchronous.

The sampled IMA ADPCM path was implemented, measured and admitted as comparison evidence. It is not the shipping backend. That reference pipeline was later retired and removed, and the streams are no longer declared in fxdata/fxdata.txt; they add no cart bytes. This is archival evidence, deliberately kept out of gen, build, run and gen-check.

8. Story

The story has two canonical editing sources:

  • story/scenes.json — scene order, titles, paragraph text, image names and sprite-sheet row names.
  • story/art.png — one opaque black/white Piskel sheet, 512×1216, with nineteen rows of four 128×64 poses.

Editing flow:

  1. Edit prose in scenes.json or artwork in art.png.
  2. Run make gen.
  3. Open docs/story-sketchbook.html for every sequence and paginated text, or the complete card sheet at docs/assets/story-cards.png.
  4. Run make gen-check, host tests and the story device suite.

The generator validates JSON, image names, duplicate rows, supported characters, empty paragraphs and over-width words. It wraps on word boundaries at twenty columns, uppercases for the native font, and emits as many six-row text pages as needed. Consecutive text pages are ordinary cards. Image cards animate four poses at 300 ms each. Cards are packed as RLE frames and shared images are packed once.

The canonical PNG may be 1-bit, palette, RGB or RGBA, including Piskel exports, but must have the exact sheet dimensions and contain only fully opaque black/white pixels. The generator never overwrites the two canonical sources. Shipping card copy is never duplicated in the HTML preview, generator or tests; the preview is generated from the same data.

Runtime semantics are intentionally modest around saves: a pending scene is a one-byte field. Acceptance writes the load and the departure scene id before playback. Continue resumes the pending scene. Finishing it clears the byte in RAM only, so a reload before the next natural checkpoint can replay it: at-least-once, not exactly-once. Delivery decks are saved before playback; survey decks are unsaved field finds. HOME is the ending prologue and resumes until the ending-presented flag is committed.

9. Resource accounting

The resource budgets are:

ResourceLimitMeasurement
Program flash29,696 B.text + .data from make size
Static SRAM1,700 B planning ceiling.data + .bss; remainder is stack/locals
Stack reserveat least 600 BPainted-stack probe above __bss_end
Cart image2 MiBfxdata/fxdata.bin, including the 4 KiB save section

LTO makes per-symbol arithmetic misleading. A change is judged on the whole image, before and after. The workflow for flash-sensitive work is:

  1. Build and record the current whole-image number.
  2. Spike the risky part.
  3. Split “implement” from “make it fit”.
  4. Measure the integrated change, not the sum of independent estimates.
  5. If it does not fit, remove or move data to the cart; do not raise the limit or claim a pass.

Moving data to FX is not free: hot cart reads cost SPI time, so only cold tables or content that already streams from the cart belong there. The final compression wave moved cold story/dock tables to FX and replaced runtime text drawing with baked stamps because those changes reduced hot-path work as well as flash.

The cart is the large store: terrain, art, story, music, text stamps and save data live there. Program flash holds code and the small tables that must stay hot. The generated layout is reviewed as an ABI, not as an incidental build artifact.

10. Working method

Work is organized with beads (bd). An epic describes a phase; child issues are bounded implement/verify units with explicit acceptance criteria and verification commands. Dependencies serialize work when tasks share a resource or generated file. The worker protocol is:

  • Read the bead and the linked contracts before editing.
  • Implement and verify in one loop; report exact commands and numbers.
  • Do not commit or push unless the orchestrator asks.
  • If it cannot fit or a gate fails, report BLOCKED with the deficit and options; never fake a pass.
  • Record durable design and measurement decisions in docs, not only in the issue.

The orchestrator reviews each diff and commits between waves. The full gate before a commit is:

make gen-check
make test
make test-tools
make docs-check
make fxtest
make fxtest-save-chain
make fxtest-save-runtime-page
make fxtest-flight
make size
make mini

For iteration, make fxtest FXTEST_ONLY=test_boot runs one device suite, and host/tooling targets can be run alone. The full gate is required for a release commit. If Ardens is missing, device targets report SKIPPED rather than a false pass; a run without captureserial is BLOCKED.

Repository conventions:

  • Generated sets are staged together after make gen.
  • Tests reference generated symbolic constants, never literal record indices.
  • Dated checkpoints go in the platform or archive docs; retired designs stay in archive/ with a superseded note.
  • Commit messages are <what> (sub-hauler-XXX.n) style for task commits.
  • The pure rules stay free of Arduino headers; device code stays free of floats, heap and String.

11. Reproducing the build

Prerequisites:

  • arduino-cli with the arduboy-homemade:avr core;
  • the sibling ../ATMlib2FX checkout for make gen and the synth library;
  • Ardens for device suites and flight timing (optional for a host-only build);
  • bd only for issue tracking, not for building.

Common commands:

make gen          # regenerate all shipping assets and headers
make gen-check    # prove generation is deterministic
make build        # FX firmware -> dist/fx
make mini         # Mini firmware -> dist/mini
make size         # whole-image flash/RAM report
make test         # host C++ tests
make test-tools   # Python tooling tests
make docs-check   # local links + selector guard
make fxtest       # 15 default device suites
make fxtest-flight
make fxtest-save-chain
make fxtest-save-runtime-page
make run          # Ardens with ELF + FX image
make debug        # developer map-inspection image
make save-migrate SAVE=/path/to/absim_<hash>.save
make render-world # overview + exact native scene pixels
make music-viewer # six-song FX jukebox in Ardens

The retired reference pipeline used the Ardens absim source to rebuild reference PCM/ADPCM and listening WAVs; it was not part of the shipping build or gen-check.

For a first read of the code, start with sub-hauler.ino, then src/app.hpp, then src/game.hpp and the view modules. For a first read of the pipeline, start with Makefile (FX_INPUTS, gen, gen-check) and tools/gen_story_beats.py. For the current limits, read platform.md; for the conventions, dev-flow.md.
